paragraphs: Dataset distillation compresses a training collection into a much smaller dataset while aiming to preserve downstream performance. Different methods construct their synthetic images in very different ways, making their success difficult to explain through a shared mechanism. This paper investigates a common ingredient: soft labels, which assign probabilities across classes instead of providing a single class label.

Through ablation experiments, the authors examine how much these labels contribute to performance. Their results identify soft labels as the main explanation for the performance of the state-of-the-art distillation methods they study. The information inside the labels matters: merely making labels probabilistic is insufficient; beneficial labels must carry structured information.

The paper also develops empirical scaling relationships between soft-label effectiveness and the number of images per class. An empirical Pareto frontier describes achievable tradeoffs in data-efficient learning. Together, these findings shift attention toward the supervision attached to distilled examples and suggest that improving label information could be a productive direction for improving distillation.
neurips-2024-a-label-is-worth-a-thousand.tldr: Ablation experiments identify structured soft labels as a major driver of the performance of the dataset distillation methods studied.

paragraphs: Long documents create two related problems for language models: fitting the material into the input and focusing on the information needed for a task. Retrieving selected passages can omit relevant material, while expanding the context window can still leave the model struggling to focus. Chain-of-Agents addresses these problems by dividing the reading and reasoning across several collaborating agents.

Worker agents handle different segments of the text and communicate sequentially through natural language. A manager agent then combines their contributions into a final response. This arrangement processes the entire input while giving each worker a shorter context. Reading and reasoning are interleaved, so information from different segments can contribute through the chain.

The authors evaluate the framework on long-context question answering, summarization, and code completion. They report improvements of up to 10% over strong retrieval-augmented, full-context, and multi-agent baselines. These results support sequential collaboration as a useful approach to long-context tasks, with the reported maximum improvement applying to the evaluated settings.
neurips-2024-chain-of-agents-large-langu.tldr: Chain-of-Agents divides long inputs among sequentially communicating workers and uses a manager to combine their reasoning.

paragraphs: Text-to-video systems can produce compelling scenes, but controlling individual characters, object movement, and viewpoints remains challenging. This paper approaches that problem by generating scene elements separately as three-dimensional representations and then composing them. A language model acts as a director, organizing the work described by the user's text.

The pipeline has four stages. First, the language model divides a complex request into descriptions of individual elements. It then invokes pretrained models to create their 3D representations. Next, multimodal language models provide rough guidance about object sizes, positions, and trajectories. Finally, information from 2D diffusion models refines the composition through score distillation sampling, helping the assembled scene better match natural-looking imagery.

Separating the elements gives the system explicit components whose placement and motion can be controlled during composition. The authors report that extensive experiments produce high-fidelity videos with flexible control over individual elements. The stated finding supports combining language-based scene planning, separate 3D generation, and diffusion-based refinement as a practical direction for controllable video generation.
neurips-2024-compositional-3d-aware-vide.tldr: An LLM directs the creation and composition of separate 3D elements, with diffusion-based refinement enabling controllable text-to-video generation.

paragraphs: Conformal prediction expresses uncertainty by returning a set of possible labels with a specified coverage probability. A useful set should contain the correct label while remaining small enough to inform a decision. Achieving coverage separately for each class can produce especially large sets when there are many classes or substantial class imbalance.

The proposed RC3P algorithm adds label-rank calibration to class-conditional conformal prediction. Standard class-conditional calibration applies class-wise score thresholding uniformly across classes. RC3P selectively applies that subroutine to a subset of classes with small class-wise top-k error. This uses information about how labels rank in the classifier's predictions to make the calibration more selective.

The authors prove class-wise coverage without tying the result to a particular classifier or data distribution, and show smaller prediction sets than the standard class-conditional method. Experiments across real-world datasets report an average set-size reduction of 26.25% while achieving class-wise coverage. The contribution is more compact uncertainty reporting while retaining a coverage target for each class.
neurips-2024-conformal-prediction-for-cl.tldr: RC3P uses label-rank calibration to reduce prediction-set sizes while providing class-wise coverage guarantees.

paragraphs: Out-of-distribution detection asks whether an input falls outside the data a model is intended to handle. One training strategy, outlier exposure, provides auxiliary examples of unfamiliar data so the detector can learn to distinguish them from ordinary inputs. This paper studies how to make better use of those auxiliary examples.

Hopfield Boosting uses modern Hopfield energy to sharpen the boundary between in-distribution data and auxiliary outliers. Its central idea is to emphasize outliers that are difficult to distinguish from familiar examples. These boundary-adjacent cases provide the training process with a focused challenge: improving separation where the distinction is currently weakest.

The authors report state-of-the-art detection performance within the outlier-exposure setting. FPR95 falls from 2.28 to 0.92 on CIFAR-10, from 11.76 to 7.94 on CIFAR-100, and from 50.74 to 36.60 on ImageNet-1K. These results support the value of directing training toward difficult auxiliary outliers. The method's stated setting includes access to auxiliary outlier data during training.
neurips-2024-energy-based-hopfield-boost.tldr: Hopfield Boosting improves outlier-exposure training by emphasizing auxiliary outliers near the detector's decision boundary.

paragraphs: A molecular conformer describes a molecule's three-dimensional arrangement. This paper generates conformers from molecular graphs through a coarse-to-fine process. It first constructs a rough arrangement at the level of molecular fragments, then generates individual atomic details while allowing the initial fragment arrangement to change.

The second stage must retain useful coarse structure while handling three-dimensional geometry consistently. Equivariant Blurring Diffusion addresses this with a forward process that progressively blurs atomic detail toward the fragment-level structure. Its reverse process reconstructs the details using equivariant networks. SE(3) equivariance means that rotating or translating the input geometry produces corresponding changes in the output geometry.

This design makes the coarse approximation a guide that can be refined alongside the atomic coordinates. The authors assess geometric and chemical quality against state-of-the-art denoising diffusion models on a benchmark of drug-like molecules and report effective generation. They also use ablations to investigate architectural choices, including the loss function and corruption process, providing evidence about how the model's design contributes to its behavior.
neurips-2024-equivariant-blurring-diffus.tldr: Equivariant Blurring Diffusion generates molecular conformers by refining fragment-level geometry into atomic detail while preserving geometric equivariance.

paragraphs: Counterfactual estimation concerns what would have happened under a different intervention within a causal model. Computing these quantities efficiently can require sampling, and the choice of sampling distribution affects how variable the estimates are. Exogenous Matching addresses this by learning proposal distributions for importance sampling in structural causal models.

The method starts from a shared upper bound for counterfactual estimators. Minimizing that bound turns the task of reducing estimator variance into a conditional distribution learning problem. This reformulation connects counterfactual estimation to existing methods for modeling conditional distributions, making those methods available for constructing useful sampling proposals.

Experiments across different types and settings of structural causal models support the theoretical results and show better counterfactual estimation than other importance sampling methods. The authors also investigate the effect of incorporating structural knowledge through counterfactual Markov boundaries. Finally, applications to identifiable proxy structural causal models demonstrate unbiased estimates. These findings support the approach's practical potential in the studied settings, including cases where estimation uses an identifiable proxy model.
neurips-2024-exogenous-matching-learning.tldr: Exogenous Matching learns importance-sampling proposals by reformulating counterfactual estimator variance reduction as conditional distribution learning.

paragraphs: Few-shot node classification requires a graph model to predict unfamiliar classes from very few labeled examples. Sharpness-Aware Minimization, or SAM, aims to improve generalization by finding flatter regions of the training loss. Its standard implementation requires two forward-backward passes per iteration, making it computationally costly.

Fast Graph SAM divides those operations between a graph neural network and a multilayer perceptron. The graph network determines the parameter perturbation, while the perceptron minimizes the perturbed loss. Reusing the gradient from the perturbation phase brings graph topology into the minimization step at almost no additional cost. A further variant, FGSAM+, performs exact perturbations periodically to improve efficiency.

Experiments show that the proposed approach outperforms standard SAM on few-shot node classification while using less computation. FGSAM+ also optimizes faster than the base optimizer in most reported cases. Competitive results on standard node classification for heterophilic graphs extend the empirical evidence beyond the few-shot setting. The findings support using different model components for SAM's two phases to balance generalization and training cost.
neurips-2024-fast-graph-sharpness-aware-.tldr: FGSAM combines graph-network perturbations with cheaper perceptron updates to improve few-shot node classification at lower training cost.

paragraphs: Stereo matching identifies corresponding content in left and right images. Although convolutional networks have improved this task, their performance can suffer when deployment images differ from training data. This paper argues that stronger attention to meaningful objects and their structure can help models generalize to unfamiliar visual domains.

The HODC framework segments objects at multiple scales and uses contrastive learning to guide feature extraction. Its dual-level loss strengthens correspondence between left and right feature regions both within a scale and across scales. The objective is to make matching depend more on semantic and structural information represented at these different levels.

HODC is applied during training and can be integrated into existing stereo networks without architectural changes. Using only synthetic training datasets, the authors report state-of-the-art generalization across multiple realistic datasets and several existing network architectures. This combination matters because it links improved transfer to a reusable training framework, with experimental evidence that the benefit is not confined to a single stereo architecture.
neurips-2024-hierarchical-object-aware-d.tldr: HODC uses object-aware contrastive training across spatial scales to improve stereo matching on unseen domains without changing network architectures.

paragraphs: Numerical distance between image pixels does not always reflect the kind of similarity useful for a task. A blurred image can remain recognizably close to its original even when a conventional distance measure ranks a noisy perturbation as closer. This paper learns Bregman divergences directly from high-dimensional data to express a different notion of image similarity.

In the demonstrated application, the learned divergence treats common corruptions such as blur as close to the original and noisy perturbations as far away. It also performs well on datasets of human perceptual similarity judgments. The authors then use the learned divergence to define adversarial attacks, replacing projected gradient descent with the corresponding mirror descent procedure.

Training with these attacks improves reported robustness to common image corruptions. For contrast corruption on CIFAR-10-C, the authors report an accuracy advantage of 27.16% over Lp-based and LPIPS-based adversarially trained networks. The results connect learning a suitable image geometry with constructing training attacks that improve robustness in the evaluated corruption setting.
neurips-2024-learning-bregman-divergence.tldr: Learned Bregman divergences provide image similarity measures that support adversarial training with improved robustness to common corruptions.

paragraphs: Out-of-distribution detectors often train with external examples standing in for the unfamiliar inputs they will eventually encounter. Those substitutes can differ from actual out-of-distribution data. The authors find this mismatch especially problematic when familiar classes are heavily imbalanced, because common and rare classes interact differently with the substitute and true outlier distributions.

AdaptOD addresses both the initial training distribution and its later adaptation. During training, a dual-normalized energy loss normalizes across classes and samples to reduce bias toward frequent classes. This produces a more balanced prediction energy and a better initial outlier distribution, while removing the need to manually tune sensitive energy-loss margins.

During inference, dynamic outlier distribution adaptation uses information from samples predicted to be out of distribution to adjust the initial distribution. The training normalization helps make that predicted set more reliable. Experiments on three benchmarks for long-tailed out-of-distribution detection show superior performance over state-of-the-art methods. The contribution combines imbalance-aware training with adaptation informed by the inputs encountered during inference.
neurips-2024-long-tailed-out-of-distribu.tldr: AdaptOD combines balanced energy-based training with inference-time adaptation to improve out-of-distribution detection under class imbalance.

paragraphs: Methods that discourage sharp training-loss behavior can have surprisingly different effects on generalization. SAM often helps, while apparently related approaches involving weight noise or gradient penalties can fail to produce similar benefits. This paper investigates those differences through the Hessian, which describes second-order changes in the loss.

The analysis separates the Hessian into a positive semidefinite Gauss-Newton component and an indefinite component called Nonlinear Modeling Error, or NME. The latter has largely been overlooked in earlier analyses. Treating these components separately allows the authors to examine information that can disappear when sharpness is considered only through the more commonly studied part.

The paper provides theoretical and empirical evidence that NME matters for gradient-penalty performance and explains sensitivity to activation functions. It also presents evidence connecting NME to performance differences between gradient penalties and weight noise. The findings argue for including this component when designing experiments and theories of sharpness regularization, because superficially similar methods can interact differently with the full loss curvature.
neurips-2024-neglected-hessian-component.tldr: A commonly overlooked Hessian component helps explain why related sharpness-regularization methods differ in their generalization benefits.

paragraphs: Instrumental-variable regression provides a strategy for identifying causal effects when unobserved factors confound the relationship of interest. In the nonparametric setting, the relationship can take flexible forms. Recent approaches have used nonlinear versions of two-stage least squares or minimax objectives; this paper develops a different optimization formulation.

The authors construct functional stochastic gradient descent that directly minimizes population risk. They provide excess-risk bounds as theoretical support and allow flexible estimator choices, including neural networks and kernel methods. The framework also accepts non-quadratic losses, which may suit structural equations beyond continuous outcomes with additive noise.

Numerical experiments show greater stability and competitive performance relative to current state-of-the-art alternatives. The paper further demonstrates how the framework handles binary outcomes, an application that has received less attention in recent nonparametric instrumental-variable work. Its contribution is therefore both an optimization route with theoretical support and a flexible modeling framework whose usefulness extends to the demonstrated binary-outcome setting.
neurips-2024-nonparametric-instrumental-.tldr: A functional stochastic-gradient approach offers stable, flexible nonparametric instrumental-variable regression, including a formulation for binary outcomes.

paragraphs: Image pyramids process an image at multiple resolutions to capture information at different spatial scales. Running the same large model at every resolution can be expensive. Parameter-Inverted Image Pyramid Networks, or PIIP, change how model capacity is assigned across those resolutions to improve the balance between computation and performance.

PIIP sends higher-resolution images through smaller networks and uses networks of different parameter sizes across the pyramid. A feature-interaction mechanism lets the resolution branches exchange information, so features at different scales can complement one another. This combination couples a different allocation of computation with explicit integration of the resulting representations.

Experiments on detection, segmentation, and classification show better performance than traditional image pyramids and single-branch networks while reducing computation. Applied to InternViT-6B, PIIP improves detection and segmentation performance by a reported 1%–2% using 40%–60% of the original computation. These results support varying model size across image resolutions as an effective architecture choice in the evaluated vision tasks.
neurips-2024-parameter-inverted-image-py.tldr: PIIP pairs higher-resolution images with smaller networks and exchanges features across scales to improve vision performance with less computation.

paragraphs: Phylogenetic inference constructs trees describing evolutionary relationships. It must determine both a discrete branching structure and continuous branch lengths, making optimization difficult. Existing approaches can be computationally burdensome or rely on pregenerated tree structures while handling topology and lengths separately, potentially overlooking useful sequence information.

PhyloGen uses a pretrained genomic language model and treats inference as tree-structure generation subject to conditions. Its feature-extraction, tree-construction, and structure-modeling modules jointly optimize topology and branch lengths. The method is presented as operating without dependence on evolutionary models or aligned-sequence constraints. A scoring function guides the optimization toward more stable gradient descent.

The authors evaluate PhyloGen on eight real-world benchmark datasets and report effectiveness and robustness. Visualizations also provide evidence of richer insight into phylogenetic relationships. The approach matters because it brings sequence representations into a unified tree-generation process, addressing the coupling between the branching pattern and branch lengths within the same framework.
neurips-2024-phylogen-language-model-enh.tldr: PhyloGen uses genomic language-model features to jointly generate and optimize phylogenetic tree topology and branch lengths.

paragraphs: Watermarking AI-generated images can support intellectual-property protection and efforts to prevent misuse. RAW introduces a framework that learns a watermark directly in image data together with a classifier trained to detect it. This changes both where the watermark is inserted and how its detectability is learned.

Existing encoder-decoder approaches described in the paper embed fixed binary codes in latent representations. RAW instead jointly trains the image-space watermark and its detector. The framework supports multiple generative architectures and allows watermark injection on the fly after training. This makes insertion usable without tying the framework to a single generative architecture.

The authors incorporate smoothing techniques to provide provable guarantees concerning a specified misclassification rate under adversarial watermark-removal attacks. Experiments use images from state-of-the-art diffusion models and report substantially faster watermark encoding and better detection under attack while preserving image quality. The contribution combines deployment flexibility, empirical attack resistance, and a formal detection guarantee; the stated guarantee concerns an error rate rather than unconditional prevention of removal.
neurips-2024-raw-a-robust-and-agile-plug.tldr: RAW jointly learns image-space watermarks and their detector, improving insertion speed and attack-resistant detection with formal error-rate guarantees.

paragraphs: Exposure assessment determines how lighting affects an image's appearance. A single score for an image or region gives limited guidance when exposure problems vary across the scene. This paper moves assessment to individual pixels, aiming to provide more precise feedback without requiring a reference image.

The proposed P-IEANet uses a Haar discrete wavelet transform to examine both lightness and image structure. The authors also introduce IEA40K, a dataset containing 40,000 images spanning 17 lighting scenarios, 27 devices, and more than 50 scenes. Each image receives dense pixel-level annotations from more than ten experts, supplying supervision for localized exposure assessment.

A benchmark compares 19 methods using the new dataset. P-IEANet achieves the best reported performance on all benchmark metrics and integrates with existing exposure-correction and lighting-enhancement methods. The model, dataset, and benchmark jointly support evaluating exposure as a spatially varying property. This makes the assessment more directly informative about where exposure-related processing is needed within an image.
neurips-2024-rethinking-no-reference-ima.tldr: P-IEANet and the densely annotated IEA40K dataset enable pixel-level exposure assessment without a reference image.

paragraphs: Scene graph generation identifies objects and their relationships. Existing open-vocabulary approaches often compare image features with fixed category descriptions. The authors argue that these unchanged descriptions struggle with relationships whose appearance varies across scenes, motivating text classifiers that respond to the visual context.

SDSGG asks a language model to analyze a scene from different roles, such as a biologist or engineer. These perspectives produce diverse scene-oriented descriptions. A renormalization mechanism then adjusts each description's influence according to its relevance to the image, rather than assigning all generated descriptions equal importance.

A lightweight mutual visual adapter complements this text-side adaptation by learning representations that account for interactions between subjects and objects. It refines CLIP's relation-recognition ability through an interaction-aware semantic space. Experiments on established benchmarks show substantial improvements over leading methods. The results support combining diverse descriptions, scene-dependent weighting, and explicit visual interaction modeling to better represent the relationships present in an image.
neurips-2024-scene-graph-generation-with.tldr: SDSGG combines role-generated scene descriptions, relevance-based weighting, and a visual adapter to improve open-vocabulary relation recognition.

paragraphs: Generating realistic time series requires modeling the patterns present in sequential data. Diffusion models have achieved strong results on this task, but the authors identify slow inference and room for better sample quality as remaining problems. SDformer explores discrete token modeling as an alternative generation approach.

The method first learns discrete representations using similarity-driven vector quantization. This maps time-series information into tokens whose representation learning is guided by similarity. A discrete Transformer then models the distribution of those tokens. The design therefore separates learning an effective token representation from learning how the represented data are distributed.

Comprehensive experiments report substantially better generated time-series quality than competing approaches while maintaining short inference time. The authors also apply the trained model directly to predictive tasks without retraining and report good results. Together, these findings suggest that the learned discrete representation and Transformer distribution model can support both generation and the demonstrated predictive uses, while addressing the inference-speed concern that motivated the work.
neurips-2024-sdformer-similarity-driven-.tldr: SDformer models similarity-based discrete time-series tokens to improve generation quality and speed, with prediction possible without retraining.

paragraphs: Interactive teaching studies how learning systems can help one another learn. Although teaching has supported methods such as data selection and distillation, its optimization principles and convergence have lacked theoretical analysis. This paper examines co-teaching as a representative case and connects it to Sharpness-Aware Minimization, or SAM.

The authors interpret co-teaching as a reduction of the larger loss landscape arising from SAM. They then formulate it as iterative parameter estimation through Expectation-Maximization. In this account, convergence comes from repeatedly improving a variational lower bound on the log marginal likelihood. That bound uses an expected log posterior over latent variables under a scaled, factorized variational distribution.

Building on the analysis, the paper introduces Sharpness Reduction Interactive Teaching, or SRIT. It incorporates generalization information from SAM into interactive teaching through a sequential optimization process. Multiple experiments validate the proposed approach's performance. The work thus links a theoretical explanation of a typical interactive-teaching process with an optimization method designed to improve its effectiveness.
neurips-2024-sharpness-aware-minimizatio.tldr: The paper connects co-teaching to SAM and Expectation-Maximization, then develops SRIT to improve interactive teaching.

paragraphs: In-context learning concerns a model's ability to use information supplied in its context to guide its behavior. Earlier theoretical work on this ability in reinforcement learning has largely addressed a single agent. This paper extends the analysis to competitive interaction, focusing on classical two-player zero-sum games.

The authors provide guarantees showing that pretrained Transformers can learn to approximate a Nash equilibrium through in-context game playing. The results cover both decentralized and centralized learning settings. Their proofs include explicit constructions demonstrating that Transformer architectures are expressive enough to realize established game-playing algorithms: decentralized V-learning and centralized VI-ULCB.

These constructions supply a concrete link between architectural capacity and the claimed learning capability. They show how known multi-agent procedures can be represented within the architecture used by pretrained models. The contribution is a theoretical demonstration of capability in the analyzed game settings, supporting a broader understanding of in-context learning when another strategic agent influences the problem.
neurips-2024-transformers-as-game-player.tldr: The paper proves that pretrained Transformers can learn approximate Nash equilibria in context for analyzed two-player zero-sum games.

paragraphs: Universal Sample Coding studies how to communicate multiple samples from an unknown distribution using few bits. The transmitter wants a receiver to generate independent, identically distributed samples from a target distribution P. Both sides have access to independent samples from a reference distribution Q, which helps support the communication procedure.

The method performs channel simulation in successive rounds and updates Q after each round. These updates aim to bring the reference distribution closer to P in KL divergence, reducing the communication required in later rounds. The authors derive a lower bound on expected communication cost and construct a practical algorithm that reaches it within a multiplicative constant.

In a federated-learning application where model updates correspond to distribution samples, the algorithm reduces communication load by 37%. The paper also reports up to a sixteenfold reduction in bits for communicating language-model samples compared with entropy-based compression. These results illustrate the potential savings from communicating samples through an adapting reference distribution across multiple rounds.
neurips-2024-universal-sample-coding-708.tldr: Updating a reference distribution across sample-communication rounds reduces bit costs, with theoretical bounds and demonstrated application savings.

paragraphs: Low-Rank Adaptation reduces fine-tuning costs by representing parameter updates through low-rank matrices. Choosing their ranks determines how much update capacity each matrix receives. SalientLoRA adapts these ranks during training, addressing the challenge of identifying important matrices while balancing allocation flexibility, stability, and efficiency.

Its salience measure tracks changes in singular-value magnitudes across multiple time steps and considers dependencies between them. Looking at this history is intended to reduce instability and randomness in importance estimates. An adaptive time window controls how much history is used for salience measurement and rank reduction. This allows rapid allocation while maintaining stability and permits higher starting ranks, expanding the available allocation space.

Experiments cover language understanding, language generation, and instruction tuning. The authors report improvements of 0.96%–3.56% over state-of-the-art methods on multiple datasets, together with a 94.5% speed improvement over AdaLoRA as allocation space expands. These findings support using training-time singular-value behavior to guide both where adaptation capacity goes and how efficiently that allocation is performed.
neurips-2024-unveiling-lora-intrinsic-ra.tldr: SalientLoRA uses singular-value histories and adaptive measurement windows to allocate LoRA ranks more effectively and efficiently.

paragraphs: Noise in a data-generation process can influence which models appear competitive. This paper asks how knowledge of noise levels can help predict whether simpler, accurate models are likely to exist. It investigates the relationship across hypothesis spaces, with particular attention to decision trees and linear models.

The authors formally show that several noise models act as implicit regularizers. They also analyze Rashomon sets, which contain models whose performance is close to optimal. Their results show that sets constructed from noisy data tend to include simpler models than corresponding sets from noise-free data. This concerns the availability of competitive simple models within those sets.

A further result shows that noise expands the collection of good features and consequently the collection of models using at least one such feature. Together, the theoretical findings offer a way to reason about model simplicity from properties of data generation. Their practical relevance is in assessing whether simple-yet-accurate models are likely to be available under the noise settings studied.
neurips-2024-using-noise-to-infer-aspect.tldr: Theoretical results connect several forms of data noise with the availability of simpler models among near-optimal alternatives.

paragraphs: Adam often trains Transformers substantially better than stochastic gradient descent, but the reason for that gap has been unclear. This paper examines the Hessian, which captures the curvature of the training loss. It identifies large differences in Hessian spectra across groups of Transformer parameters, calling this pattern block heterogeneity.

The authors investigate Transformers, convolutional networks, multilayer perceptrons, and quadratic problems. They find that SGD can match Adam on problems without this heterogeneity, while performing worse when the heterogeneity is present. These comparisons connect the optimizer gap to differences between parameter blocks rather than treating it solely as an unexplained property of Transformers.

An initial theoretical analysis points to SGD's shared learning rate: one rate cannot adequately handle the differing behavior of heterogeneous blocks. Coordinate-wise learning rates, as used by Adam, could alleviate that limitation. The contribution combines empirical comparisons with an initial explanation of why adaptive step sizes can help in these settings; it does not establish that every Transformer requires Adam.
neurips-2024-why-transformers-need-adam-.tldr: Differences in loss curvature across parameter blocks help explain Adam's advantage over SGD in the Transformer settings studied.
